articles.summary: Nomination day opened the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, kicking off a 14-day campaign ahead of polling on August 1. Nearly 890,000 voters are registered, with early voting set for July 28. The contest follows Barisan Nasional's landslide win over Anwar Ibrahim's Pakatan Harapan in the earlier Johor state election.
articles.title: Negeri Sembilan election kicks off with nomination day for 16th state polls

articles.summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim made his first campaign appearance for the Negeri Sembilan state election, attending events in Ampangan, Paroi and Sikamat to rally support for the incumbent Pakatan Harapan state government. The visit is widely seen as an attempt to regain momentum after the coalition's heavy defeat in the recent Johor state election.
articles.title: Anwar launches Negeri Sembilan campaign push for Pakatan Harapan

articles.summary: Coverage from the Asia ESG Summit 2026 in Selangor examines how Malaysia is moving from voluntary ESG pledges toward mandatory sustainability disclosure under the Securities Commission's National Sustainability Reporting Framework. Panellists discussed gaps between corporate ESG claims and measurable environmental outcomes as reporting rules tighten for listed companies.
articles.title: Malaysia pushes for tangible ESG compliance as sustainability reporting expands

articles.summary: Plantation group SD Guthrie and WWF-Malaysia announced an expanded conservation and sustainability collaboration in Sabah aimed at protecting biodiversity and supporting responsible land-use practices. The partnership reflects growing pressure on Malaysia's plantation sector to align with tightening environmental and ESG standards.
articles.title: SD Guthrie and WWF-Malaysia expand sustainability partnership in Sabah

articles.summary: Strong labour demand is pushing up staff turnover, with high-skilled workers making up the largest share of retrenchments between 2021 and 2025. Displaced workers are being reabsorbed quickly, with 1.5 job placements recorded for every worker retrenched so far in 2026, as firms compete for scarce skilled talent amid a dynamic investment environment.
articles.title: Labour demand drives higher staff turnover in Malaysia

articles.summary: Following the Cabinet's decision to make Perkeso's Lindung 24/7 accident-protection scheme voluntary rather than mandatory, employees who do not want the automatic salary deduction must file an exemption form. The scheme extends social security coverage to accidents occurring outside working hours, funded through worker contributions starting at 0.75% of monthly wages.
articles.title: Workers must submit exemption form to opt out of Lindung 24/7 scheme

articles.summary: Malaysia is finalising a National Climate Change Bill that would make it roughly the 60th country worldwide, and one of the first in Southeast Asia, with dedicated climate legislation. The law would establish a regulatory body overseeing carbon reduction mechanisms, climate governance and data reporting as the government works toward its net-zero 2050 target.
articles.title: Malaysia set to join nations with dedicated climate change law

articles.summary: A Selangor state executive councillor said intense rainfall combined with river capacity limits and ongoing embankment repair works caused the flash floods that swamped Petaling Jaya and parts of the Klang Valley on July 18. The incident renewed scrutiny of urban flood resilience as Malaysia's monsoon season brings increasingly intense downpours.
articles.title: Selangor blames heavy rain, local factors for Petaling Jaya flash floods

articles.summary: Malaysia's National AI Office (NAIO) will be formally empowered on July 28 to coordinate AI governance and strategy nationwide, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo has confirmed. NAIO will work alongside existing regulators to oversee AI safeguards while driving the country's broader ambition to rank among the top 20 AI-ready nations by 2030.
articles.title: Malaysia's National AI Office to be formally empowered from July 28

articles.summary: The National AI Office released a public consultation paper on July 10 setting out proposed components of Malaysia's AI Governance Bill, including a new AI regulatory authority and design requirements for AI systems. Stakeholder submissions are due by July 31, ahead of a planned legal framework governing AI development and deployment in the country.
articles.title: Public consultation on Malaysia's AI Governance Bill nears close

articles.summary: Google launched Gemini 3.6 Flash alongside Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and a new Flash Cyber model built for cybersecurity tasks, while teasing an eventual Gemini 4 release. The new Flash model cuts output token usage by about 17%, lowers pricing, and improves coding and computer-use benchmark scores compared with its predecessor.
articles.title: Google releases Gemini 3.6 Flash and two other new models
